speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you please describe the exact location and character of your sudden abdominal pain? Also, has this pain radiated to your back or groin, and did it start before or after you ate?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent heart attack, are you currently experiencing shortness of breath, or does the pain feel worse when you take a deep breath? Also, has your abdominal pain migrated from the center to your lower right side, or does it feel constant and severe?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe abdominal pain. I also have Bloody loose bowel movements, No vomiting, Sudden onset.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent heart attack and bloody bowel movements, does your pain feel disproportionate to the physical exam, and are you currently experiencing dizziness or a racing heart? I also need to know if you have a history of irregular heartbeat or if anyone in your family has had vascular issues.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known diabetes mellitus for 35 years and hypertension for 20 years. History of acute myocardial infarction. Social history: Smokes 15–20 cigarettes per day for the past 40 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: CT Angiography of the Abdomen.

Given your heavy smoking history, recent heart attack, and severe pain with bloody stools, I suspect a vascular emergency and need to visualize your mesenteric arteries immediately.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia
